Introduction
Approximately one in eight Americans is over the age of 65. By 2030, 72.1 million Americans will 
be 85 years or older, representing 19 percent of the population. Women will continue to out number 
men and by 2030, Hispanics, Asians/Pacific Islanders, Native Americans, and African-Americans 
are projected to represent approximately 25 percent of the elderly population. Specific nutrition 
concerns for older adults include eating habits, eating ability, managing meals, relationships, 
culture, financial resources, and social support. Nutrition-related problems stem from chronic 
diseases, depression, dementia, dysphagia, obesity, cachexia, and frailty. Nutrition programs will 
have to become more diverse and flexible to meet the needs of this ever-growing older population.
